2025-11-19.summary: Your first full day behind the glasses. You set retention to 30 days and local-first on before leaving home, then practice the one-tap pause at the bakery counter and the hardware till, and end the evening deleting clips on purpose.

hl_20251119_2.caption: You tapped pause by accident at the third stop, laughed at yourself, and tapped it back on.

hl_20251119_4.caption: The bakery has a small notice about recording, so you tapped pause and kept it off through the queue.

hl_20251119_5.caption: You paused again at the till out of habit, then stood outside to check the count of paused minutes.

hl_20251126_1.caption: Rain hit sideways and you stood watching it for a while with your tea going cold.

hl_20251126_2.caption: You lifted the boards onto battens and found the damp had only reached one corner.

hl_20251126_3.caption: You agreed to bring the radio for Pip and one thing for the table, nothing more.

hl_20251126_4.caption: The case went back on and the station came through clear on the first turn of the dial.

hl_20251126_5.title: Settings check
hl_20251126_5.caption: You confirmed retention and local-first were both still where you set them, then put the glasses down.

hl_20251127_1.caption: You paused at the counter out of habit and the cashier slid the boxes over with a nod.

hl_20251127_2.title: Line 4 across town
hl_20251127_2.caption: The tram was crowded with covered dishes and you held the radio on your knees.

hl_20251127_4.caption: He found two stations by himself and then kept going until he found a third.

hl_20251127_5.caption: You washed and your brother-in-law dried, and the glasses stayed paused on the sideboard through the whole thing.

hl_20251127_6.title: Ride home, resumed
hl_20251127_6.caption: You turned recording back on at the tram stop and let it run the wet ride home.

hl_20251128_1.caption: You drank two cups of tea and put the glasses on ten minutes later than usual.

hl_20251128_2.title: Chairs reassembled
hl_20251128_2.caption: Both frames went back square and you sat on each one before calling it done.

hl_20251128_3.caption: She plugged it in at her kitchen table, found her station, and handed you a jar of preserves.

hl_20251128_4.caption: You paused at the counter, then stood outside with the loaf talking about the storm.

hl_20251128_5.caption: The app pointed to a clip of the bench, and the tape was under it, next to a spilled screw jar.

hl_20251221_3.caption: You tip the jar out on a tray and sort brass from steel while a record plays low.

2025-12-22.summary: Ines's cabinet hinge finally sits flush, Sis calls to plan Christmas Eve, and you end the day gluing a wedge into a drying rack that was never meant to wobble.
2025-12-22.one_line: Ines's cabinet hinge finally sits flush, Sis calls to plan Christmas Eve, and you end the day gluing a wedge into a drying rack that was never meant to wobble.

hl_20251222_1.title: Cabinet hinge, third attempt
hl_20251222_1.caption: The hinge sits flush at last after you shave the recess by two millimetres and reset the screws.

hl_20251222_2.title: Call from Sis
hl_20251222_2.caption: She asks what time you'll come on the twenty-fourth and warns that the tree lights died again.

hl_20251222_3.title: More glue sticks
hl_20251222_3.caption: You buy a pack of glue sticks and a roll of narrow tape the counter keeps behind the register.

hl_20251222_4.title: Drying rack rescue
hl_20251222_4.caption: At home you glue a wedge into the wobbling drying rack and hang the tote by the door for tomorrow.

2025-12-23.summary: Fog swallows the street all day. A parcel arrives, the library is nearly empty, and you wrap the last gifts while the bakery smells stay in your coat.
2025-12-23.one_line: Fog swallows the street all day.

hl_20251223_1.title: Parcel at the door
hl_20251223_1.caption: The mail carrier hands over a small parcel of brass fittings and says the fog is worse by the harbor.

hl_20251223_2.title: Last buns before the holiday
hl_20251223_2.caption: You buy a paper bag of buns and the counter slips an extra one in, saying it's the last of the tray.

hl_20251223_3.title: Fog-light reading
hl_20251223_3.caption: Almost nobody is in the library; you read two chapters about lamp wiring with your glasses slipping down.

hl_20251223_4.title: Tram through the fog
hl_20251223_4.caption: Line 4 crawls along the waterfront and the fog turns the streetlamps into soft circles.

hl_20251223_5.title: Last wrapping
hl_20251223_5.caption: You finish the final parcel, cross off the list, and set the toolbox by the door for tomorrow.

2025-12-24.summary: Christmas Eve at Sis's house: you spread the rescued fairy lights across the kitchen table, and Pip finds the corroded socket that has been killing the whole string.
2025-12-24.one_line: Christmas Eve at Sis's house: you spread the rescued fairy lights across the kitchen table, and Pip finds the corroded socket that has been killing the whole string.

hl_20251224_1.title: Crossing town with tools
hl_20251224_1.caption: The tote holds the coiled lights, the multimeter, and a small box of spare bulbs; the tram is nearly empty.

hl_20251224_2.title: Lights across the kitchen table
hl_20251224_2.caption: You lay the whole string out on the big table and test each section with the multimeter while Sis makes tea.

hl_20251224_3.title: Pip finds the bad socket
hl_20251224_3.caption: Pip spots the green-crusted socket halfway down the string and is allowed to hold the screwdriver.

hl_20251224_4.title: Two spare bulbs and a taped wire
hl_20251224_4.caption: You swap two bulbs and tape the repaired wire; the string lights up and Pip insists on testing it three times.

hl_20251224_5.title: Dov's kitchen
hl_20251224_5.caption: Recording pauses for dinner: Dov cooks far too much and the kitchen smells of butter and orange peel.

hl_20251224_6.title: Tree lit, slow blink
hl_20251224_6.caption: The tree is lit at last, blinking slowly enough that Pip lies under it counting the dark bulbs.

2025-12-25.summary: A quiet Christmas to yourself: coffee, a walk to the park through loose snow flurries, a long call with Sis and Pip, and Mrs. Okafor knocking with a plate of food.
2025-12-25.one_line: A quiet Christmas to yourself: coffee, a walk to the park through loose snow flurries, a long call with Sis and Pip, and Mrs.

hl_20251225_1.title: Slow morning coffee
hl_20251225_1.caption: You sit under the desk lamp with coffee and the library book, in no hurry to be anywhere.

hl_20251225_2.title: Flurries at the duck pond
hl_20251225_2.caption: Loose snow flurries melt as they land; the ducks look unimpressed and the paths are almost empty.

hl_20251225_3.title: Call with Sis and Pip
hl_20251225_3.caption: Pip describes every present in detail and Sis says the tree lights have stayed on all morning.

hl_20251225_4.title: A plate at the door
hl_20251225_4.caption: Mrs. Okafor brings a plate of rice and fried plantain and refuses to take the plate back empty.

2025-12-26.summary: Rain drums on the garage roof all day while you give the oak dresser its final coat and finally sort the screw jar into labeled jars.
2025-12-26.one_line: Rain drums on the garage roof all day while you give the oak dresser its final coat and finally sort the screw jar into labeled jars.

hl_20251226_1.title: Final coat on the dresser
hl_20251226_1.caption: You wipe the dresser down, check the drawer gaps with the tape, and start the last thin coat.

hl_20251226_2.title: Screw jar gets labeled
hl_20251226_2.caption: The jar's contents get sorted into four smaller jars with paper labels written in pencil.

hl_20251226_3.title: Rainy hardware run
hl_20251226_3.caption: You dash out for felt pads and come back damp, with the bag held under your coat.

hl_20251226_4.title: Invoice and a list
hl_20251226_4.caption: At home you write out the invoice for the dresser and start a list for the new year.

2025-12-27.summary: A quiet repair cafe between the holidays: only a handful of visitors, June from the bookbinding class with a wobbly stool, and Tomas tuning a radio for the fun of it.
2025-12-27.one_line: A quiet repair cafe between the holidays: only a handful of visitors, June from the bookbinding class with a wobbly stool, and Tomas tuning a radio for the fun of it.

hl_20251227_1.title: Small turnout, open bench
hl_20251227_1.caption: The hall is cold and half the tables stay folded; the mentor puts the kettle on twice.

hl_20251227_2.title: June's wobbly stool
hl_20251227_2.caption: June brings a stool from the bookbinding class; you glue and wedge the leg while she describes the new binding press.

hl_20251227_3.title: Loaves for the table
hl_20251227_3.caption: You collect the two loaves the bakery held back and slice one for the volunteers.

hl_20251227_4.title: Radio tuning for fun
hl_20251227_4.caption: With nobody waiting, Tomas tunes the radio to a station playing something old and the hall feels warmer.

2025-12-28.summary: Laps at the pool, a grey walk through the park, and an evening where you ask the app where the tape measure went and find it in the tote.
2025-12-28.one_line: Laps at the pool, a grey walk through the park, and an evening where you ask the app where the tape measure went and find it in the tote.

hl_20251228_1.title: Four lengths, no rush
hl_20251228_1.caption: The pool is almost empty and the coach lets you swim without drills, just counting strokes.

hl_20251228_2.title: Grey loop of the pond
hl_20251228_2.caption: You meet Mrs. Okafor on the path and walk one loop together, comparing leftover food.

hl_20251228_3.title: Where did the tape measure go
hl_20251228_3.caption: You ask the app where you last had the yellow tape and it points you to the tote by the door.

hl_20251228_4.title: Year-end page
hl_20251228_4.caption: Under the desk lamp you start a page listing what to fix, sell, and give away before spring.

uncertain.text: You may have left the reading glasses at the pool again rather than at home (low confidence).

2025-12-29.summary: Dov lends a van and you deliver the finished oak dresser to Hollis, who asks you to pause recording at the door; the rest of the day is felt pads and a careful invoice.
2025-12-29.one_line: Dov lends a van and you deliver the finished oak dresser to Hollis, who asks you to pause recording at the door; the rest of the day is felt pads and a careful invoice.

hl_20251229_1.title: Blankets and a borrowed van
hl_20251229_1.caption: Dov backs the van up to the garage door and you wrap the dresser in two old blankets.

hl_20251229_2.title: Drop-off and a pause
hl_20251229_2.caption: Hollis asks you to stop recording at the door, so the handover happens off the record; the dresser fits the alcove exactly.

hl_20251229_3.title: Felt pads and small screws
hl_20251229_3.caption: You buy a pack of felt pads and a box of small screws for the next job on the bench.

hl_20251229_4.title: Tram home, lighter tote
hl_20251229_4.caption: The tote is nearly empty on the way home, just the notebook and a folded blanket.

2025-12-30.summary: Errands before New Year: a bakery order for tomorrow, cheese and apples at the market, a late parcel from the mail carrier, and Pip's gift wrapped twice.
2025-12-30.one_line: Errands before New Year: a bakery order for tomorrow, cheese and apples at the market, a late parcel from the mail carrier, and Pip's gift wrapped twice.

hl_20251230_1.title: Order for tomorrow
hl_20251230_1.caption: You order a loaf and a tray of buns for New Year's Eve and the counter writes it on a slip.

hl_20251230_2.title: Cheese and apples
hl_20251230_2.caption: You buy a hard cheese and a bag of apples at the market and Mrs. Okafor adds a jar of preserve to your bag.

hl_20251230_3.title: Late parcel
hl_20251230_3.caption: The mail carrier brings a parcel that had been sitting at the depot and apologizes for the delay.

hl_20251230_4.title: Pip's gift, wrapped twice
hl_20251230_4.caption: You wrap Pip's gift, decide the paper is wrong, unwrap it, and rewrap it with the glue gun for the ribbon ends.

2025-12-31.summary: New Year's Eve at Sis's house: you fix a wobbly chair leg while Pip holds the lamp, Dov cooks too much again, and the year ends with a countdown at the kitchen table.
2025-12-31.one_line: New Year's Eve at Sis's house: you fix a wobbly chair leg while Pip holds the lamp, Dov cooks too much again, and the year ends with a countdown at the kitchen table.

hl_20251231_1.title: Across town with a plate
hl_20251231_1.caption: You ride line 4 with the tote of small tools and a plate of buns balanced on your knees.

hl_20251231_2.title: Dov's kitchen, again
hl_20251231_2.caption: Dov is already cooking three things at once and Sis clears the big table for the evening.

hl_20251231_3.title: Wobbly chair leg, Pip holding the lamp
hl_20251231_3.caption: Pip holds the desk lamp steady on the floor while you glue and press the chair leg back into its socket.

hl_20251231_4.title: Card game and a scoring page
hl_20251231_4.caption: Pip wins two rounds of a card game and insists on keeping score himself in the notebook.

hl_20251231_5.title: Countdown at the table
hl_20251231_5.caption: The tree lights stay on through the countdown and everyone clinks glasses at the kitchen table.

uncertain.text: You may have left the yellow tape measure on Sis's kitchen table rather than in the tote (low confidence).

2026-01-01.summary: You start the year slowly: coffee, a frost-furred window, three lines in the paper notebook. The resolution is small and stubborn — learn to solder properly before the year turns again.
2026-01-01.one_line: You start the year slowly: coffee, a frost-furred window, three lines in the paper notebook.

hl_20260101_1.title: First page of the year
hl_20260101_1.caption: You write three lines in the paper notebook: solder, finish the oak dresser, keep Saturdays free.

hl_20260101_2.title: Frost on the duck pond
hl_20260101_2.caption: The pond has thin ice at the edges and the ducks keep to the middle; you walk the path twice to stay warm.

hl_20260101_3.title: New year call with Sis
hl_20260101_3.caption: Sis talks over the noise of Dov's kitchen and you promise to come for dinner next week.

2026-01-02.summary: You spend the morning sanding the water-marked top of Hollis's oak dresser at the garage workshop. On the way home you buy a multimeter and a reel of solder, which makes the resolution feel like it has a budget.
2026-01-02.one_line: You spend the morning sanding the water-marked top of Hollis's oak dresser at the garage workshop.

hl_20260102_1.title: Dresser top, third pass
hl_20260102_1.caption: You measure the drawer runner with the yellow tape and write the number in the notebook.

hl_20260102_2.title: A multimeter of your own
hl_20260102_2.caption: The person behind the counter explains the dial twice; you buy the cheapest one that beeps.

hl_20260102_3.title: Tram line 4, window seat
hl_20260102_3.caption: The tote sits on your knees with sandpaper dust working its way through the canvas.

hl_20260102_4.title: Rye loaf before it sells out
hl_20260102_4.caption: The shelf is nearly empty and the cashier saves you the last dark loaf.

uncertain.text: The multimeter receipt may be in the wallet rather than the tote (low confidence).

2026-01-03.summary: First repair cafe of the year: you carry the metal desk lamp in and the mentor walks you through testing the switch. Recording paused for twenty-five minutes when a visitor asked you to switch the glasses off while she talked.
2026-01-03.one_line: First repair cafe of the year: you carry the metal desk lamp in and the mentor walks you through testing the switch.

hl_20260103_1.title: The lamp on the bench
hl_20260103_1.caption: The red toolbox comes out of the cupboard and the lamp finally gets opened up.

hl_20260103_2.title: Tomas and the radio dial
hl_20260103_2.caption: Tomas has three radios on his end of the table and asks you to hold the aerial steady.

hl_20260103_3.title: Stacking chairs at the end
hl_20260103_3.caption: You stay to fold tables and find three odd screws under the radiator.

hl_20260103_4.title: Lamp working on the way home
hl_20260103_4.caption: You switch the repaired lamp on in the tram and a stranger nods at the glow.

2026-01-04.summary: Sunday swim in a cold pool; the coach lets you finish the last length alone. You walk to the bakery afterwards with wet hair and buy cinnamon buns while the morning is still hard and bright.
2026-01-04.one_line: Sunday swim in a cold pool; the coach lets you finish the last length alone.

hl_20260104_1.title: Six lengths before the water gets busy
hl_20260104_1.caption: The coach watches from the shallow end and says your elbow is dropping on the left.

hl_20260104_2.title: Cinnamon buns, still warm
hl_20260104_2.caption: You eat one on the way home and carry the bag with both hands against the cold.

hl_20260104_3.title: Keys back on the hook
hl_20260104_3.caption: You ask the app where the keys went and it points to the coat pocket, not the hallway hook.

uncertain.text: The umbrella may still be by the pool entrance (low confidence).

2026-01-05.summary: The glue gun goes missing somewhere between the kitchen and the workshop, and it is the first time you ask out loud: where did I put the glue gun? It turns up in the canvas tote by the door.
2026-01-05.one_line: The glue gun goes missing somewhere between the kitchen and the workshop, and it is the first time you ask out loud: where did I put the glue gun?

hl_20260105_1.title: Where did I put the glue gun
hl_20260105_1.caption: The answer comes back as the tote by the door — you carried it home on Saturday and forgot.

hl_20260105_2.title: Drawer runners, second coat
hl_20260105_2.caption: You sketch the runner profile in the notebook so you don't measure it a fourth time.

hl_20260105_3.title: Sandpaper by the sheet
hl_20260105_3.caption: You buy four sheets of fine grit and a small brush and talk to nobody.

hl_20260105_4.title: Reading the multimeter manual
hl_20260105_4.caption: You prop it against the salt jar and read the same page three times.

2026-01-06.summary: Second soldering session: you melt a wire's insulation and singe a fingertip, but one joint holds cleanly. The multimeter beeps in the right places and you stop while you are ahead.
2026-01-06.one_line: Second soldering session: you melt a wire's insulation and singe a fingertip, but one joint holds cleanly.

hl_20260106_1.title: Beeping in the right places
hl_20260106_1.caption: You test the practice board and write the readings in the notebook with cold hands.

hl_20260106_2.title: A joint that actually holds
hl_20260106_2.caption: Third attempt: the solder flows and sits shiny instead of beading up.

hl_20260106_3.title: Fingertip under the cold tap
hl_20260106_3.caption: You run the burn under water and eat dinner standing up.

2026-01-07.summary: Fog all morning and the town sounds muffled. At the library you return two books and see a poster for a January bookbinding workshop, so you sign up at the holds desk before you can talk yourself out of it.
2026-01-07.one_line: Fog all morning and the town sounds muffled.

hl_20260107_1.title: Signing up for bookbinding
hl_20260107_1.caption: The holds desk staff circle the first date on the poster and you copy it into the notebook.

hl_20260107_2.title: Two books on furniture finishes
hl_20260107_2.caption: You read standing up in the aisle and take only one home.

hl_20260107_3.title: Fog on tram line 4
hl_20260107_3.caption: The umbrella drips onto the floor and the tram smells of wet wool.

uncertain.text: The library card may have gone into the coat pocket instead of the wallet (low confidence).

2026-01-08.summary: Dinner at Sis's: Dov cooks a long-simmered stew and Pip brings out a broken torch he wants fixed by spring. You take it home in the tote, promising a new switch.
2026-01-08.one_line: Dinner at Sis's: Dov cooks a long-simmered stew and Pip brings out a broken torch he wants fixed by spring.

hl_20260108_1.title: Tram across town, windy
hl_20260108_1.caption: The tram leans at the corner and everyone on board looks up at once.

hl_20260108_2.title: Dov's stew on the stove
hl_20260108_2.caption: He lifts the lid and the whole kitchen fills with steam.

hl_20260108_3.title: Pip's broken torch
hl_20260108_3.caption: He hands it over with strict instructions: it must work again before spring.

hl_20260108_4.title: Washing up and plans
hl_20260108_4.caption: Sis asks about the resolution and laughs when you say solder, then says she is proud.

uncertain.text: The torch may have been left on the kitchen table instead of in the tote (low confidence).

2026-01-09.summary: Errands on foot: sandpaper and a toggle switch at the corner hardware store, a rye loaf at Quill Street, a short chat with the mail carrier about the icy steps. A few flakes come down and melt on contact.
2026-01-09.one_line: Errands on foot: sandpaper and a toggle switch at the corner hardware store, a rye loaf at Quill Street, a short chat with the mail carrier about the icy steps.

hl_20260109_1.title: Mail on the step
hl_20260109_1.caption: The mail carrier warns you about the icy step and you salt it before going out.

hl_20260109_2.title: A toggle switch for Pip's torch
hl_20260109_2.caption: You hold three sizes against your palm and pick the middle one.

hl_20260109_3.title: Rye loaf and a cinnamon bun
hl_20260109_3.caption: The cashier remembers the dark loaf and sets one aside before you ask.

hl_20260109_4.title: Umbrella found behind the door
hl_20260109_4.caption: You ask the app where the umbrella went; it has been behind the door since Tuesday.

uncertain.text: The multimeter may have been left at the workshop rather than brought home (low confidence).

2026-01-10.summary: First bookbinding workshop at the library: you fold signatures badly and meet June, who has done it before. In the afternoon you drop into the repair cafe for an hour and the desk lamp goes back together working.
2026-01-10.one_line: First bookbinding workshop at the library: you fold signatures badly and meet June, who has done it before.

hl_20260110_1.title: First signature folded wrong
hl_20260110_1.caption: June from across the table shows you how to crease with a folder and says everyone's first attempt looks like that.

hl_20260110_2.title: Pressing the spine under weight
hl_20260110_2.caption: You stack three heavy books on the glued spine and write the time in the notebook so you don't forget it.

hl_20260110_3.title: An hour at the repair cafe
hl_20260110_3.caption: The lamp goes back together and the mentor says your soldering has improved since last week.

hl_20260110_4.title: Glasses left on the library table
hl_20260110_4.caption: You ask the app where the reading glasses went and it says the workshop table in the second room.

hl_20260110_5.title: Tram home in the cold
hl_20260110_5.caption: The tote holds a lopsided booklet and you keep checking it hasn't unfolded.

2026-01-11.summary: Cold bright Sunday: six lengths, one note from the coach about your left elbow. At home you fold more signatures at the kitchen table and press the booklet under a stack of boards.
2026-01-11.one_line: Cold bright Sunday: six lengths, one note from the coach about your left elbow.

hl_20260111_1.title: Six lengths in cold water
hl_20260111_1.caption: The coach times the last one and does not say whether it was good.

hl_20260111_2.title: Folding signatures at the kitchen table
hl_20260111_2.caption: You fold eight pages, get six right, and write the trick in the notebook.

hl_20260111_3.title: Ducks and bitter sunshine
hl_20260111_3.caption: The pond path is salted and the ducks are loud; you walk to the far bench and back.

2026-01-12.summary: The oak dresser is finished and Hollis actually gasps at the top. Recording paused for fifteen minutes while she talked about her mother's house; afterwards you carried the dresser out to her car together.
2026-01-12.one_line: The oak dresser is finished and Hollis actually gasps at the top.

hl_20260112_1.title: Last of the drawer runners
hl_20260112_1.caption: Two screws short, and the jar on the bench happens to have exactly two left.

hl_20260112_2.title: Hollis sees the top
hl_20260112_2.caption: She runs a palm across the refinished oak and says it looks like a different piece of furniture.

hl_20260112_3.title: Loading the dresser into the car
hl_20260112_3.caption: You wrap the corners in blankets and the two of you slide it into the back seat.

hl_20260112_4.title: Quiet evening under the desk lamp
hl_20260112_4.caption: You write the dresser's finish recipe in the notebook so you can repeat it.

uncertain.text: The spare workshop key may be in the wallet rather than on the brass ring (low confidence).

2026-01-13.summary: You solder the new switch into Pip's torch, using the repaired desk lamp as a task light. The multimeter reads clean, and the torch lights on the second try.
2026-01-13.one_line: You solder the new switch into Pip's torch, using the repaired desk lamp as a task light.

hl_20260113_1.title: Torch on the bench
hl_20260113_1.caption: The desk lamp shines straight down on the open torch and you test the old switch first.

hl_20260113_2.title: Switch soldered, second try
hl_20260113_2.caption: The first joint bridges two contacts; the second is neat and the torch lights.

hl_20260113_3.title: Sketching the wiring in the notebook
hl_20260113_3.caption: You draw the torch circuit from memory and label the switch pins.

2026-01-14.summary: Mrs. Okafor's planters have split along the rim, so you take two home to glue and clamp. Later the Larsen kids borrow the umbrella for the park and bring it back folded wrong.

hl_20260114_1.title: Two split planters on the kitchen floor
hl_20260114_1.caption: Mrs. Okafor carries them over and stays to watch the glue gun warm up.

hl_20260114_2.title: Clamped and drying
hl_20260114_2.caption: You clamp both rims and leave them by the radiator, smelling faintly of hot glue.

hl_20260114_3.title: Ducks and a borrowed umbrella
hl_20260114_3.caption: The Larsen kids run ahead to the pond and return the umbrella inside out.

hl_20260114_4.title: Planters back over the wall
hl_20260114_4.caption: You carry them next door and she gives you a jar of preserved lemons in return.

uncertain.text: The clamps may have been left on the kitchen sill rather than put away (low confidence).

2026-01-15.summary: Back at the library you return the finishing books and take out one on bookbinding. Halfway through the month the resolution is holding: three soldered joints, one finished dresser, one badly folded booklet.
2026-01-15.one_line: Back at the library you return the finishing books and take out one on bookbinding.

hl_20260115_1.title: Returning the finishing books
hl_20260115_1.caption: The holds desk staff renews nothing but stamps the card and points you at the craft shelf.

hl_20260115_2.title: June in the newspaper room
hl_20260115_2.caption: She is reading with a magnifier and reminds you to bring your folded booklet next week.

hl_20260115_3.title: Coffee and a bun before the tram
hl_20260115_3.caption: You sit by the window and watch the street get grey.

hl_20260115_4.title: Three resolutions, annotated
hl_20260115_4.caption: You cross nothing out but add a note beside 'solder properly': keep practising, ask the mentor for a harder job.

uncertain.text: The library card may have been left at the holds desk rather than slipped into the wallet (low confidence).

2026-01-16.summary: Frost on the tram windows all the way to the workshop; you spent the day sanding the oak dresser's drawers and stopped at the bakery for a rye loaf on the way home.
2026-01-16.one_line: Frost on the tram windows all the way to the workshop; you spent the day sanding the oak dresser's drawers and stopped at the bakery for a rye loaf on the way home.

hl_20260116_1.title: Frosted tram windows
hl_20260116_1.caption: You rubbed a circle clear with your sleeve and watched the harbor go white at the edges.

hl_20260116_2.title: Dresser drawers, third pass
hl_20260116_2.caption: Third sanding pass on the oak drawer fronts, tape measure out to check they still sit square.

hl_20260116_3.title: Rye loaf and a cinnamon bun
hl_20260116_3.caption: The bakery was warm enough that you stood a minute longer than you needed to.

hl_20260116_4.title: Call with Sis about Sunday
hl_20260116_4.caption: She confirmed lunch at hers on Sunday and said Dov is already planning something with lentils.

hl_20260116_5.title: Wiring sketch before bed
hl_20260116_5.caption: You drew the lamp circuit from memory in the notebook, then crossed most of it out.

2026-01-17.summary: You finally bought a multimeter at the corner hardware store and spent the afternoon at the repair cafe learning to solder properly, tinning and re-tinning the same length of wire until it looked neat.
2026-01-17.one_line: You finally bought a multimeter at the corner hardware store and spent the afternoon at the repair cafe learning to solder properly, tinning and re-tinning the same length of wire until it looked neat.

hl_20260117_1.title: Multimeter, finally
hl_20260117_1.caption: You compared two meters on the counter and took the one with the clearer dial and the simpler probes.

hl_20260117_2.title: First proper soldering practice
hl_20260117_2.caption: Your mentor showed you how to tin the tip, then had you solder and desolder the same wire six times.

hl_20260117_3.title: Tomas's radio, one cold joint
hl_20260117_3.caption: Tomas found a cracked solder joint on a radio board and let you reflow it under his thumb's direction.

hl_20260117_4.title: Continuity checks with the new meter
hl_20260117_4.caption: You beeped out three suspected breaks and wrote each result in the notebook with the wire colour.

hl_20260117_5.title: Ride home with solder on your fingers
hl_20260117_5.caption: Your fingertips smelled of flux the whole way home and you kept checking the joints in your head.

2026-01-18.summary: Sunday swim, then lunch across town at Sis's where Dov had a pot of lentil soup going and Pip showed you a toy with a broken winding key.
2026-01-18.one_line: Sunday swim, then lunch across town at Sis's where Dov had a pot of lentil soup going and Pip showed you a toy with a broken winding key.

hl_20260118_1.title: Coach fixes your kick
hl_20260118_1.caption: Coach had you do four slow lengths just on the kick, and by the last one it actually felt different.

hl_20260118_2.title: Dov's lentil soup
hl_20260118_2.caption: Dov served it with bread he'd made that morning and refused to say what was in it.

hl_20260118_3.title: Pip's winding key
hl_20260118_3.caption: Pip handed you a tin toy with a bent winding key and watched your face while you looked at it.

hl_20260118_4.title: Tram home in the grey
hl_20260118_4.caption: You got a seat by the door and dozed most of the way back with the umbrella dripping on your knee.

2026-01-19.summary: Ines dropped off two chairs at the workshop and you spent the day stripping old varnish, with a damp tram ride home and a notebook list of soldering things to practise.
2026-01-19.one_line: Ines dropped off two chairs at the workshop and you spent the day stripping old varnish, with a damp tram ride home and a notebook list of soldering things to practise.

hl_20260119_1.title: Ines brings two chairs
hl_20260119_1.caption: She carried one in each hand and apologised for the state of the seats, which were honestly not that bad.

hl_20260119_2.title: Stripping old varnish
hl_20260119_2.caption: You scraped and sanded one chair back down to bare wood and found a repair someone had made decades ago.

hl_20260119_3.title: Damp ride to the hardware store
hl_20260119_3.caption: The tram was steamy and crowded and you got off two stops early just to walk in the drizzle.

hl_20260119_4.title: List of things to solder
hl_20260119_4.caption: You wrote five small things to practise next Saturday, starting with a wire splice and ending with the lamp switch.

2026-01-20.summary: You lost the glue gun somewhere between the kitchen table and the workshop bench and asked the app for the first time, then found it under a rag.
2026-01-20.one_line: You lost the glue gun somewhere between the kitchen table and the workshop bench and asked the app for the first time, then found it under a rag.

hl_20260120_1.title: Where did I put the glue gun
hl_20260120_1.caption: You asked the app out loud, felt slightly silly, and got a list of three places it had last seen the glue gun.

hl_20260120_2.title: Under a rag, on the bench
hl_20260120_2.caption: It was under an oily rag on the workshop bench, still warm, exactly as the last place suggested.

hl_20260120_3.title: Fog and a cinnamon bun
hl_20260120_3.caption: The fog was so thick the bakery windows were white and the cashier said the ferries had stopped.

hl_20260120_4.title: Glue gun and meter on the same bench
hl_20260120_4.caption: You glued a loose chair spline and then tested the meter's leads on themselves until it beeped.

hl_20260120_5.title: Prep for the bookbinding evening
hl_20260120_5.caption: You found the class reminder and wrote June's name in the notebook so you would remember it at the library.

2026-01-21.summary: Morning on the chairs, an afternoon at the library for holds, and the evening bookbinding workshop where you sat next to June and learned a simple pamphlet stitch.
2026-01-21.one_line: Morning on the chairs, an afternoon at the library for holds, and the evening bookbinding workshop where you sat next to June and learned a simple pamphlet stitch.

hl_20260121_1.title: Second chair stripped
hl_20260121_1.caption: You got the second chair down to bare wood faster than the first and measured the seat rails out of habit.

hl_20260121_2.title: Holds desk and a new card sleeve
hl_20260121_2.caption: The holds desk had your reserved book and a fresh plastic sleeve for the library card, which had gone soft at the corner.

hl_20260121_3.title: Pamphlet stitch with June
hl_20260121_3.caption: June from the class had brought her own awl and talked you through the stitching holes without once making you feel slow.

hl_20260121_4.title: Home with a small booklet
hl_20260121_4.caption: You carried your first stitched booklet home in the tote and kept taking it out to check the spine.

2026-01-22.summary: A hard frost, a parcel of glue sticks, screws from the corner hardware store, and a small bracket repair for Mrs. Okafor's planters before the afternoon in the workshop.
2026-01-22.one_line: A hard frost, a parcel of glue sticks, screws from the corner hardware store, and a small bracket repair for Mrs.

hl_20260122_1.title: Mail carrier and a parcel
hl_20260122_1.caption: The mail carrier handed over a small parcel of glue sticks and warned you the path was slick.

hl_20260122_2.title: Topping up the screw jar
hl_20260122_2.caption: You bought a bag of assorted small screws and poured them into the jar at the workshop counter.

hl_20260122_3.title: Chairs get their first coat
hl_20260122_3.caption: First thin coat on both chairs, and you moved the old desk lamp closer to see the grain.

hl_20260122_4.title: Planter bracket for Mrs. Okafor
hl_20260122_4.caption: One of her planter brackets had pulled out of the wall and you swapped the screws for longer ones.

hl_20260122_5.title: Cold loop past the duck pond
hl_20260122_5.caption: You walked the short loop past the pond, where the water was mostly ice at the edges and nobody else was out.

2026-01-23.summary: A windy day finishing the chairs and taking a call from Hollis about the oak dresser; you ended up at the bakery twice and bought nothing the second time.
2026-01-23.one_line: A windy day finishing the chairs and taking a call from Hollis about the oak dresser; you ended up at the bakery twice and bought nothing the second time.

hl_20260123_1.title: Second coat and a wobble
hl_20260123_1.caption: Second coat went on well, but one chair still rocked a few millimetres and the tape measure confirmed it.

hl_20260123_2.title: Hollis calls about the dresser
hl_20260123_2.caption: Hollis asked whether the drawers could be ready next week and you wrote the day down twice.

hl_20260123_3.title: Rye loaf, then back again
hl_20260123_3.caption: You bought a rye loaf at lunch and came back at four just to stand out of the wind.

hl_20260123_4.title: Tram doors fighting the wind
hl_20260123_4.caption: The tram doors struggled against the gusts and everyone on board laughed about it at the same time.

hl_20260123_5.title: Gluing a spline by lamplight
hl_20260123_5.caption: You glued the loose spline on a spare chair part just to have something to clamp overnight.

2026-01-24.summary: A busy repair cafe Saturday: someone brought in a metal desk lamp with a broken switch, and with your mentor watching you soldered the new contact in yourself.
2026-01-24.one_line: A busy repair cafe Saturday: someone brought in a metal desk lamp with a broken switch, and with your mentor watching you soldered the new contact in yourself.

hl_20260124_1.title: Desk lamp with a broken switch
hl_20260124_1.caption: A visitor set a heavy metal desk lamp on the bench and said it only worked if you held the switch just so.

hl_20260124_2.title: Continuity test, then your own solder joint
hl_20260124_2.caption: The meter showed the switch was intermittent; you removed the old contact and soldered a new one with your mentor only watching.

hl_20260124_3.title: Tomas's radio plays again
hl_20260124_3.caption: Tomas's radio came back to life mid-afternoon and he insisted on leaving it on for the rest of the session.

hl_20260124_4.title: Lamp still flickers — take it home
hl_20260124_4.caption: The lamp worked but flickered when warm, so you bagged it to finish at the workshop and told the visitor you'd call.

uncertain.text: The flicker may be the flex rather than the switch (low confidence).

2026-01-25.summary: Cold bright Sunday: swim, then a walk around the duck pond with Pip, who insisted on counting the ducks twice and got different numbers.
2026-01-25.one_line: Cold bright Sunday: swim, then a walk around the duck pond with Pip, who insisted on counting the ducks twice and got different numbers.

hl_20260125_1.title: Four lengths, no board
hl_20260125_1.caption: Coach took the board away and made you swim four lengths with the new kick, and you did not drown.

hl_20260125_2.title: Counting ducks twice
hl_20260125_2.caption: Pip counted fourteen ducks, then eleven, and decided the difference was because some had gone home for lunch.

hl_20260125_3.title: Late lunch and a bent key
hl_20260125_3.caption: You straightened Pip's winding key at the kitchen table and told him it would hold until spring if he was gentle.

hl_20260125_4.title: Lamp base on the kitchen table
hl_20260125_4.caption: You opened the lamp base again at home and flexed the cord while watching the meter needle.

2026-01-26.summary: Hollis collected the oak dresser and paid in full, and you spent the afternoon starting the seating on Ines's chairs with a lighter heart than usual.
2026-01-26.one_line: Hollis collected the oak dresser and paid in full, and you spent the afternoon starting the seating on Ines's chairs with a lighter heart than usual.

hl_20260126_1.title: Loading the dresser drawers
hl_20260126_1.caption: Hollis's car boot took the drawers one at a time, each wrapped in a blanket that did not quite fit.

hl_20260126_2.title: Paid in full, and a photo
hl_20260126_2.caption: Hollis paid the agreed amount and took a photo of the dresser before driving off carefully.

hl_20260126_3.title: Starting the chair seats
hl_20260126_3.caption: You took the old seat pads off and labelled every screw by chair so nothing got swapped.

hl_20260126_4.title: Texting Sis the photo
hl_20260126_4.caption: You sent Sis a photo of the finished dresser and she replied with far too many exclamation marks.

2026-01-27.summary: Fog all day and a quiet hunt for the tape measure, which the app found folded into the canvas tote; you picked up a held book and worked slowly on the chair seats.
2026-01-27.one_line: Fog all day and a quiet hunt for the tape measure, which the app found folded into the canvas tote; you picked up a held book and worked slowly on the chair seats.

hl_20260127_1.title: Tape measure in the tote
hl_20260127_1.caption: You asked the app where the tape measure had gone and it turned up folded into the bottom of the canvas tote.

hl_20260127_2.title: Held book and a quiet corner
hl_20260127_2.caption: The holds desk had your book and you read twenty pages in the corner chair before you noticed the time.

hl_20260127_3.title: Chair seat foam cut and glued
hl_20260127_3.caption: You cut new foam for both seats and glued the edges down with the glue gun, working slowly and badly at first.

hl_20260127_4.title: Fog on the tram line
hl_20260127_4.caption: The tram went slow through the fog and the conductor announced each stop twice, which nobody minded.

uncertain.text: The tape measure may have been in the tote since Saturday rather than since Tuesday (low confidence).

2026-01-28.summary: A restless cold day of small jobs: a hinge screw for a neighbour, two failed attempts at a neat solder joint, and a long walk to the bakery to shake it off.
2026-01-28.one_line: A restless cold day of small jobs: a hinge screw for a neighbour, two failed attempts at a neat solder joint, and a long walk to the bakery to shake it off.

hl_20260128_1.title: Hinge screws, wrong size twice
hl_20260128_1.caption: You bought the wrong length hinge screws, went back, and the second lot were also wrong.

hl_20260128_2.title: Two bad solder joints
hl_20260128_2.caption: You tried a neater joint on a practice wire twice and both times used too much solder, which the meter did not care about but you did.

hl_20260128_3.title: Cabinet hinge for Mrs. Okafor
hl_20260128_3.caption: Her kitchen cabinet hinge had been loose for weeks and the third size of screw finally bit properly.

hl_20260128_4.title: Long way round to the bakery
hl_20260128_4.caption: You walked the long way to the bakery in the cold, bought nothing sweet, and felt better anyway.

hl_20260128_5.title: Glue gun and a list of failures
hl_20260128_5.caption: You wrote down what went wrong with the joints in the notebook, which was more useful than sulking.

2026-01-29.summary: Quiet day: chair seats finished, a second stitched booklet at home in the evening, and a message from June about the next bookbinding class.
2026-01-29.one_line: Quiet day: chair seats finished, a second stitched booklet at home in the evening, and a message from June about the next bookbinding class.

hl_20260129_1.title: Seats tacked down
hl_20260129_1.caption: Both seat pads went on straight and you checked the corners with the tape measure more times than necessary.

hl_20260129_2.title: Returning the held book
hl_20260129_2.caption: You returned the book a day early and the holds desk staff said that never happens.

hl_20260129_3.title: Second booklet, steadier stitching
hl_20260129_3.caption: Your stitching holes were straighter this time, and June messaged to say the next class is in February.

2026-01-30.summary: You chased the flicker in the desk lamp down to the flex, replaced it, and the lamp has now stayed lit for an hour straight with the meter clipped on.
2026-01-30.one_line: You chased the flicker in the desk lamp down to the flex, replaced it, and the lamp has now stayed lit for an hour straight with the meter clipped on.

hl_20260130_1.title: Flex, not switch
hl_20260130_1.caption: You wiggled the flex with the meter attached and the needle dropped exactly where the old cord had been bent.

hl_20260130_2.title: New flex, soldered properly
hl_20260130_2.caption: You soldered the new flex in with a small neat joint first time and had to look at it twice to believe it.

hl_20260130_3.title: Mentor's phone verdict
hl_20260130_3.caption: Your mentor said over the phone that if it holds for an hour it will hold, and to check the strain relief anyway.

hl_20260130_4.title: Cinnamon bun worth the walk
hl_20260130_4.caption: You walked to the bakery in the last of the sun and ate the bun outside because you did not want to go in yet.

2026-01-31.summary: Last day of the month at the repair cafe, where the desk lamp went home working and the Larsen kids brought in a toy that needed two screws and a lesson in gentleness.
2026-01-31.one_line: Last day of the month at the repair cafe, where the desk lamp went home working and the Larsen kids brought in a toy that needed two screws and a lesson in gentleness.

hl_20260131_1.title: The lamp goes home lit
hl_20260131_1.caption: The visitor plugged the lamp in, flicked the switch once, and it stayed on while they carried it out.

hl_20260131_2.title: The Larsen kids and a loose toy
hl_20260131_2.caption: Two kids from across the street brought a toy with a rattling inside and you let them hold the screw jar while you opened it.

hl_20260131_3.title: Teaching the meter to a beginner
hl_20260131_3.caption: You showed a nervous first-timer how to use the multimeter on a dead kettle before anyone touched the inside of it.

hl_20260131_4.title: Packing up slowly
hl_20260131_4.caption: Tomas packed the radios away one by one and your mentor said you'd stop burning solder tips soon enough.

hl_20260131_5.title: Tram home with the tote heavier
hl_20260131_5.caption: The tote was heavier going home than coming out, mostly because of a jar of screws someone insisted you take.

uncertain.text: One small screw from the toy may have gone under the bench rather than back in the jar (low confidence).

2026-02-01.summary: A gray Sunday: you walk to the park under drizzle, then eat a late lunch at your sister's big kitchen while your nephew folds a paper boat.
2026-02-01.one_line: A gray Sunday: you walk to the park under drizzle, then eat a late lunch at your sister's big kitchen while your nephew folds a paper boat.

hl_20260201_1.title: Tea and a dresser list
hl_20260201_1.caption: You sit by the window with tea, reading glasses on, and sketch the dresser drawer order in the paper notebook.

hl_20260201_2.title: Umbrella located
hl_20260201_2.caption: You ask the app where the dark folding umbrella went and find it behind the door, then take it to the park.

hl_20260201_3.title: Duck pond in drizzle
hl_20260201_3.caption: The drizzle keeps most walkers away; you watch two ducks circle the pond with the umbrella low over your shoulder.

hl_20260201_4.title: Late lunch at sister's
hl_20260201_4.caption: Your sister's kitchen smells of soup; your nephew shows you a paper boat while your brother-in-law ladles lunch.

hl_20260201_5.title: Measuring the shelf
hl_20260201_5.caption: Back home, you check the shelf width with the yellow tape and leave the desk lamp on while the rain softens.

2026-02-02.summary: Rain follows you on tram line 4 to the workshop, where the oak dresser's top comes apart in slow stages; you stop at the bakery for rye on the way home.
2026-02-02.one_line: Rain follows you on tram line 4 to the workshop, where the oak dresser's top comes apart in slow stages; you stop at the bakery for rye on the way home.

hl_20260202_1.title: Wet tram window
hl_20260202_1.caption: You board line 4 with the dark umbrella dripping; the brass key ring with the blue tag sits in your coat pocket.

hl_20260202_2.title: Dresser top loosened
hl_20260202_2.caption: The client's oak dresser top lifts after you slide the yellow tape along the joint and mark screw positions with pencil.

hl_20260202_3.title: Screw jar sort
hl_20260202_3.caption: You sort the jar of assorted screws by length into the notebook's list, pausing recording when a client asks about the finish.

hl_20260202_4.title: Rye loaf stop
hl_20260202_4.caption: At the bakery counter you pay with the brown wallet and take a rye loaf, keeping the receipt tucked in the paper bag.

hl_20260202_5.title: Glue and tape question
hl_20260202_5.caption: You ask the app where the tape measure went and find it under the dresser; a small glue repair waits on the bench.

2026-02-03.summary: A windy day splits between the workshop and the corner hardware store; the dresser drawers get new runners, and you pause recording when the client stops by to talk budget.
2026-02-03.one_line: A windy day splits between the workshop and the corner hardware store; the dresser drawers get new runners, and you pause recording when the client stops by to talk budget.

hl_20260203_1.title: Runner dry-fit
hl_20260203_1.caption: You dry-fit new drawer runners against the dresser, checking each gap with the yellow tape until the lines match.

hl_20260203_2.title: Hardware errand
hl_20260203_2.caption: At the corner store you buy a short strip of sandpaper and a handful of small screws for the screw jar.

hl_20260203_3.title: Client budget pause
hl_20260203_3.caption: The client stops by; you pause recording while you talk through the budget and write the agreed finish in the notebook.

hl_20260203_4.title: Glue gun at the bench
hl_20260203_4.caption: You run a thin bead from the glue gun along a loose veneer edge and clamp it while the wind rattles the garage door.

hl_20260203_5.title: Windy tram ride
hl_20260203_5.caption: On tram line 4 the dark umbrella folds badly in the wind; you keep the blue-tag keys in your hand until home.

2026-02-04.summary: A library afternoon: you renew holds, trade bookbinding notes with a classmate, and carry a stack of repair manuals home on the tram.
2026-02-04.one_line: A library afternoon: you renew holds, trade bookbinding notes with a classmate, and carry a stack of repair manuals home on the tram.

hl_20260204_1.title: Holds desk renewal
hl_20260204_1.caption: At the holds desk you show the library card and pick up two repair manuals on drawer joinery.

hl_20260204_2.title: Bookbinding notes
hl_20260204_2.caption: Your bookbinding classmate pages through your notebook, and you copy a stitching diagram into the margin.

hl_20260204_3.title: Cinnamon bun lunch
hl_20260204_3.caption: You buy a cinnamon bun at the bakery counter and eat it on a bench while the overcast stays dry.

hl_20260204_4.title: Tote full of manuals
hl_20260204_4.caption: Before boarding, you ask the app where the library card went and find it in the canvas tote pocket; tram line 4 hums through gray streets.

hl_20260204_5.title: Evening index
hl_20260204_5.caption: At home you put on the reading glasses and index the manuals under the desk lamp, marking pages with scraps.

2026-02-05.summary: Fog sits over the street while you fit drawer runners; a multimeter check on the workshop lamp turns into a small detour before you close early.
2026-02-05.one_line: Fog sits over the street while you fit drawer runners; a multimeter check on the workshop lamp turns into a small detour before you close early.

hl_20260205_1.title: Foggy bench start
hl_20260205_1.caption: Fog softens the garage windows as you line up screws from the jar along the dresser's new drawer runners.

hl_20260205_2.title: Lamp detour
hl_20260205_2.caption: You clip the multimeter to the repaired desk lamp, find a loose solder joint, and stop to fix it before the drawers.

hl_20260205_3.title: Forgotten lunch
hl_20260205_3.caption: You walk home through fog for lunch, leaving the dark umbrella by the door and the wallet on the hall shelf.

hl_20260205_4.title: Veneer clamp
hl_20260205_4.caption: Back at the bench, you ask the app where the tape measure is and find it under a clamp; glue sets along the veneer.

hl_20260205_5.title: Short hardware run
hl_20260205_5.caption: You make a short run to the corner store for two longer screws, then lock the workshop before the fog thickens.

uncertain.text: The multimeter may have been returned to the red toolbox, not the bench drawer (low confidence).

2026-02-06.summary: A wet errand day: bakery, a short call with your sister about Sunday, and an evening sorting screws at home while rain taps the window.
2026-02-06.one_line: A wet errand day: bakery, a short call with your sister about Sunday, and an evening sorting screws at home while rain taps the window.

hl_20260206_1.title: Rye and buns
hl_20260206_1.caption: At the bakery counter you pay for rye bread and two cinnamon buns, tucking the change into the brown wallet.

hl_20260206_2.title: Drizzle on line 4
hl_20260206_2.caption: Tram line 4 is steamy; your dark umbrella drips by your boots and the blue-tag keys warm in your pocket.

hl_20260206_3.title: Call about Sunday
hl_20260206_3.caption: Your sister calls about Sunday lunch; you hear your nephew in the background asking whether you will bring the paper boat.

hl_20260206_4.title: Screw sorting at home
hl_20260206_4.caption: You spread the screw jar on a cloth and sort lengths into the notebook while rain taps the window.

hl_20260206_5.title: Lamp and list
hl_20260206_5.caption: Under the repaired desk lamp you finish the list for Monday and set the reading glasses on top of the notebook.

2026-02-08.summary: A cold swim, a slow breakfast, then a visit to the neighbor's planters to return a borrowed trowel; the desk lamp glows on the repair bench by evening.
2026-02-08.one_line: A cold swim, a slow breakfast, then a visit to the neighbor's planters to return a borrowed trowel; the desk lamp glows on the repair bench by evening.

hl_20260208_1.title: Sunday laps
hl_20260208_1.caption: The swim coach counts your laps from the pool edge; you keep the brown wallet in a locker and the water is cold.

hl_20260208_2.title: Warm breakfast
hl_20260208_2.caption: At home you make toast under the repaired desk lamp's glow, reading glasses still fogged from the pool.

hl_20260208_3.title: Planters and trowel
hl_20260208_3.caption: Your neighbor knocks about a borrowed trowel and plant saucer; you talk by the door while the cold snap holds.

hl_20260208_4.title: Duck pond cold
hl_20260208_4.caption: You walk to the duck pond under a pale cold sky, dark umbrella closed, while kids across the street race ahead.

hl_20260208_5.title: Lamp on the bench
hl_20260208_5.caption: At home you check the desk lamp's switch with the tape measure as a straight edge and leave it glowing over the bench.

2026-02-09.summary: You wake with a scratchy throat, keep the workshop closed, and visit the neighborhood clinic; the glasses come off for the next two days and recording pauses in the exam room.
2026-02-09.one_line: You wake with a scratchy throat, keep the workshop closed, and visit the neighborhood clinic; the glasses come off for the next two days and recording pauses in the exam room.

hl_20260209_1.title: Scratchy throat
hl_20260209_1.caption: You wake with a sore throat, set the reading glasses on the shelf, and sip tea while rain starts outside.

hl_20260209_2.title: Cancel the day
hl_20260209_2.caption: You send a message to the dresser client to postpone, then put the wallet and blue-tag keys into the canvas tote.

hl_20260209_3.title: Clinic visit pause
hl_20260209_3.caption: At the neighborhood clinic you pause recording at the desk; a nurse checks your temperature and advises rest and fluids.

hl_20260209_4.title: Ride home
hl_20260209_4.caption: You take tram line 4 home with the dark umbrella across your knees, feeling the cold settle behind your eyes.

hl_20260209_5.title: Glasses off
hl_20260209_5.caption: At home you put the reading glasses in the drawer for the next two days and leave the desk lamp off while you rest.

2026-02-10.summary: Paused all day: home sick, glasses on the charger.
2026-02-10.one_line: Paused all day: home sick, glasses on the charger.

2026-02-11.summary: Paused all day: home sick, glasses on the charger.
2026-02-11.one_line: Paused all day: home sick, glasses on the charger.

2026-02-12.summary: Still a little foggy-headed, you ask the app where your reading glasses went and find them behind the tea tin; a short workshop session is enough for one day.
2026-02-12.one_line: Still a little foggy-headed, you ask the app where your reading glasses went and find them behind the tea tin; a short workshop session is enough for one day.

hl_20260212_1.title: Glasses found
hl_20260212_1.caption: You ask the app where the reading glasses went and find them behind the tea tin, then put them on for the first time in two days.

hl_20260212_2.title: First tram back
hl_20260212_2.caption: Tram line 4 feels loud after two days indoors; you keep the dark umbrella closed and the blue-tag keys in your palm.

hl_20260212_3.title: Soft roll
hl_20260212_3.caption: At the bakery counter you buy a soft roll and eat half before the workshop, still coughing into your elbow.

hl_20260212_4.title: Light dresser work
hl_20260212_4.caption: You sand one dresser drawer lightly, then pause recording when the client calls to check on the schedule.

hl_20260212_5.title: Early close
hl_20260212_5.caption: You measure the last drawer gap with the yellow tape and close the workshop early, leaving the desk lamp off.
