2026-07-08.summary: Fog sat on the town all morning; you fixed a wobbly newspaper shelf at the library, ran into June from the bookbinding class, and watered Sis's garden in the quiet.
2026-07-08.one_line: Fog sat on the town all morning; you fixed a wobbly newspaper shelf at the library, ran into June from the bookbinding class, and watered Sis's garden in the quiet.

hl_20260708_1.title: Fog and a warm paper bag
hl_20260708_1.caption: The bakery was the only bright thing on the street; you took a loaf and ate a bun standing outside.

hl_20260708_2.title: Wobbly newspaper shelf
hl_20260708_2.caption: The holds desk staff showed you the shelf by the reading chairs, and you tightened the bracket with two screws from the jar.

hl_20260708_3.title: June from bookbinding
hl_20260708_3.caption: June was returning a stack of novels and asked whether you still had the bone folder she lent you in January.

hl_20260708_4.title: Quiet house, ticking clock
hl_20260708_4.caption: You watered, wrote the day in the notebook at the big kitchen table, and left before dark came down.

2026-07-09.summary: Ines's chair frames got their first coat of finish, Hollis rang about delivery, and you came home smelling of solvent and cold water.
2026-07-09.one_line: Ines's chair frames got their first coat of finish, Hollis rang about delivery, and you came home smelling of solvent and cold water.

hl_20260709_1.title: Brushes and more glue sticks
hl_20260709_1.caption: You bought two brushes and a fistful of glue sticks, and the shop had finally restocked the fine sandpaper.

hl_20260709_2.title: First coat on the chair frames
hl_20260709_2.caption: The frames went from grey-brown to warm honey in one pass, and you hung them from a wire to dry.

hl_20260709_3.title: Hollis on the phone
hl_20260709_3.caption: Hollis asked whether the dresser could come Wednesday, and you said yes before checking the drying time.

hl_20260709_4.title: Lists under the desk lamp
hl_20260709_4.caption: A cold shower, then the notebook, then the lamp switched off at half nine.

2026-07-10.summary: Night market on the harbor with string lights and grilled corn; you went with Mrs. Okafor and the Larsen kids, ran into Tomas, and walked home along the water.
2026-07-10.one_line: Night market on the harbor with string lights and grilled corn; you went with Mrs.

hl_20260710_1.title: Short morning in the garage
hl_20260710_1.caption: You stopped sanding at eleven because of the heat, and found the wallet at the bottom of the tote before leaving.

hl_20260710_2.title: String lights over the harbor
hl_20260710_2.caption: The market filled the quayside with stalls, and the kids went straight for the fried dough.

hl_20260710_3.title: Grilled corn and radio talk
hl_20260710_3.caption: Tomas turned up with a bag of old radio dials and talked about Saturday's bench while you ate corn.

hl_20260710_4.title: Walk along the water
hl_20260710_4.caption: Recording paused for twenty minutes when a stall holder asked you to, then you walked the long way back with the neighbor.

2026-07-11.summary: The repair cafe was packed — six fans, a kettle, and a lamp with a broken switch — and afterwards you watered Sis's garden in the empty house.
2026-07-11.one_line: The repair cafe was packed — six fans, a kettle, and a lamp with a broken switch — and afterwards you watered Sis's garden in the empty house.

hl_20260711_1.title: Six fans on two tables
hl_20260711_1.caption: Every second person brought a fan; the mentor took the oldest one apart and let a teenager hold the screwdriver.

hl_20260711_2.title: A lamp with a broken switch
hl_20260711_2.caption: A couple brought a lamp they said had been in the family for years; you swapped the switch and it lit first time.

hl_20260711_3.title: Radio dials and the screw jar
hl_20260711_3.caption: Tomas fixed two radios and you refilled the screw jar from a bag of mixed hardware someone donated.

hl_20260711_4.title: Watering the empty house
hl_20260711_4.caption: You watered the tomatoes and brought in the post, and the neighbor's cat followed you up the path.

uncertain.text: The multimeter may have been left at the hall rather than packed away (low confidence).

2026-07-12.summary: Morning laps, then Sis's family came back from their trip and Dov cooked again; Pip's scooter sat in the hallway with a soft wheel waiting for you.
2026-07-12.one_line: Morning laps, then Sis's family came back from their trip and Dov cooked again; Pip's scooter sat in the hallway with a soft wheel waiting for you.

hl_20260712_1.title: Sunday laps
hl_20260712_1.caption: Cloud cover kept the pool quiet and the coach let you swim an extra set without saying anything.

hl_20260712_2.title: Last check before they arrive
hl_20260712_2.caption: You watered, opened the windows, and propped the scooter wheel off the floor so it wouldn't flat-spot.

hl_20260712_3.title: They came back loud
hl_20260712_3.caption: Dov cooked a huge pot of something, Sis unpacked, and Pip asked when you could fix the wheel.

hl_20260712_4.title: Own bed again
hl_20260712_4.caption: You hung the keys on the hook, dropped the tote by the door, and slept with the window open.

2026-07-13.summary: A slow Monday: three coats of oil on Hollis's dresser, a call to confirm Wednesday, and an early night with the fan going.
2026-07-13.one_line: A slow Monday: three coats of oil on Hollis's dresser, a call to confirm Wednesday, and an early night with the fan going.

hl_20260713_1.title: Bun on the way in
hl_20260713_1.caption: You ate a cinnamon bun on the tram and got sugar on the tote strap, which you noticed much later.

hl_20260713_2.title: Three coats of oil
hl_20260713_2.caption: The oak drank the oil in patches at first, then went even and dark and good under your hand.

hl_20260713_3.title: Confirming Wednesday
hl_20260713_3.caption: Hollis confirmed the delivery window and asked if the drawers still smelled of cedar; you said you'd check.

hl_20260713_4.title: Early night
hl_20260713_4.caption: You wrote two lines in the notebook, turned off the desk lamp, and lay in front of the fan.

2026-07-15.summary: You delivered the oak dresser to Hollis in a borrowed van, returned your library books, and bought a bun to mark the end of the job.
2026-07-15.one_line: You delivered the oak dresser to Hollis in a borrowed van, returned your library books, and bought a bun to mark the end of the job.

hl_20260715_1.title: Wrapping the dresser
hl_20260715_1.caption: You wrapped the corners in an old blanket and checked each drawer for the cedar smell Hollis asked about.

hl_20260715_2.title: Roped into the van, then the front room
hl_20260715_2.caption: You tied the dresser upright in the borrowed van, drove across town, and it slid into Hollis's front room on the first try.

hl_20260715_3.title: Returns at the holds desk
hl_20260715_3.caption: You returned both books and the staff member asked whether the newspaper shelf was still holding.

hl_20260715_4.title: A bun for the end of a job
hl_20260715_4.caption: You sat on the low wall outside with a bun and the smell of the day's wood still on your hands.

2026-07-16.summary: A hot Thursday at the bench: you spend the morning re-waxing the oak dresser's drawer runners, then ride the tram home with a rye loaf and your shirt sleeves rolled to the elbow.
2026-07-16.one_line: A hot Thursday at the bench: you spend the morning re-waxing the oak dresser's drawer runners, then ride the tram home with a rye loaf and your shirt sleeves rolled to the elbow.

hl_20260716_1.title: Tram before the heat
hl_20260716_1.caption: The 7:15 is half empty; you stand with the canvas tote between your feet and watch the harbour glare through the open windows.

hl_20260716_2.title: Runners scraped, waxed, set aside
hl_20260716_2.caption: The yellow tape measure had slid under the bottom shelf; you asked the app where you last had it and found it in a minute.

hl_20260716_3.title: Rye loaf and two buns
hl_20260716_3.caption: The bakery is stifling and smells of yeast; you take the dark rye and two cinnamon buns and pay without lingering.

hl_20260716_4.title: Watering the planters next door
hl_20260716_4.caption: Mrs. Okafor is away for two days, so you fill her watering can twice and leave it under the tap.

hl_20260716_5.title: Notes on the lamp switch
hl_20260716_5.caption: Under the repaired desk lamp you sketch a wiring note for Saturday and add sandpaper to tomorrow's list.

uncertain.text: Keys may have been left in the workshop lock for a while mid-morning (low confidence).

2026-07-17.summary: You glue a chair frame in the morning, then ride the tram to the harbour for the first night market of the summer with Sis, Dov and Pip, eating fried bread while the light goes orange.
2026-07-17.one_line: You glue a chair frame in the morning, then ride the tram to the harbour for the first night market of the summer with Sis, Dov and Pip, eating fried bread while the light goes orange.

hl_20260717_1.title: Chair frame glued and clamped
hl_20260717_1.caption: The second of Ines's chairs gets its loose joint cleaned and glued, four clamps holding it square on the bench.

hl_20260717_2.title: Shutters closed against the heat
hl_20260717_2.caption: You close the shutters, drink a lot of water and lie on the floor for twenty minutes with the desk lamp off.

hl_20260717_3.title: Night market, lanterns over the fish stalls
hl_20260717_3.caption: Paper lanterns go up along the harbour wall and Pip runs ahead between crates of ice and trays of peaches.

hl_20260717_4.title: The paper fan goes missing
hl_20260717_4.caption: Pip loses his fan within ten minutes; you ask the app where you last saw it and it turns up under the dumpling stall's bench.

hl_20260717_5.title: Fried bread and a fiddle
hl_20260717_5.caption: Dov finds a table by the water and you eat fried bread with sugar while someone plays a fiddle badly and happily.

2026-07-18.summary: Paused all day: a guest asked not to be recorded.
2026-07-18.one_line: Paused all day: a guest asked not to be recorded.

2026-07-19.summary: Paused all day: a guest asked not to be recorded.
2026-07-19.one_line: Paused all day: a guest asked not to be recorded.

2026-07-20.summary: First day of house-sitting: you wake in Sis's big kitchen, meet the mail carrier at the gate, water the tomato pots, and still put in a few hours at your own bench in the afternoon.
2026-07-20.one_line: First day of house-sitting: you wake in Sis's big kitchen, meet the mail carrier at the gate, water the tomato pots, and still put in a few hours at your own bench in the afternoon.

hl_20260720_1.title: Two bags on the tram line 4
hl_20260720_1.caption: You ride across town with two bags, a folded umbrella you probably won't need, and the house keys on the blue tag ring.

hl_20260720_2.title: Coffee in a kitchen that isn't yours
hl_20260720_2.caption: Dov leaves a pot of coffee and a note about the bins before heading to work, and you drink it standing at the counter.

hl_20260720_3.title: A parcel at the gate
hl_20260720_3.caption: The mail carrier knocks with a parcel for Sis and takes the two letters you hand over.

hl_20260720_4.title: Two hours at the bench
hl_20260720_4.caption: You measure Ines's cabinet doors, note the hinge sizes, and leave a clamped chair to cure overnight.

hl_20260720_5.title: Tomato pots and a hose
hl_20260720_5.caption: Pip helps water the pots and soaks his shoes, and you find the app remembers which pot needed the extra can.

uncertain.text: The parcel may have been for the neighbours (low confidence).

2026-07-21.summary: A bench day: you strip a chair seat, buy sandpaper and glue sticks at the corner hardware store, and Ines brings the second chair over in the afternoon heat.
2026-07-21.one_line: A bench day: you strip a chair seat, buy sandpaper and glue sticks at the corner hardware store, and Ines brings the second chair over in the afternoon heat.

hl_20260721_1.title: Seat stripped back to the frame
hl_20260721_1.caption: The old seat cover comes off with a dull knife and the frame underneath is sound, which is the good news of the morning.

hl_20260721_2.title: Sandpaper, glue sticks, two hinges
hl_20260721_2.caption: The corner store is narrow and cool; you buy three grades of sandpaper and a bag of mixed screws for the repair cafe jar.

hl_20260721_3.title: Ines brings the second chair
hl_20260721_3.caption: Ines arrives with the chair in the back of her car and stays ten minutes talking about her grandmother's cabinets.

hl_20260721_4.title: Notes at the big kitchen table
hl_20260721_4.caption: With glasses on you write up the hinge measurements and ask the app how many hours you logged on the dresser in June.

2026-07-22.summary: Library day: you pick up two holds, run into June from the bookbinding class, and end up promising a mending table for the library's August workshop.
2026-07-22.one_line: Library day: you pick up two holds, run into June from the bookbinding class, and end up promising a mending table for the library's August workshop.

hl_20260722_1.title: Two holds at the desk
hl_20260722_1.caption: The holds desk hands over a book on veneers and one on small motors; your card had been in the canvas tote all along.

hl_20260722_2.title: June from the bookbinding class
hl_20260722_2.caption: June is returning a torn atlas and asks whether you'd show her how to mend a hinge at the August workshop.

hl_20260722_3.title: Iced coffee and a slice
hl_20260722_3.caption: You take the corner table by the window and read the motor book with the iced coffee sweating onto a napkin.

hl_20260722_4.title: Cold noodles and a fan
hl_20260722_4.caption: Sis makes cold noodles, the table fan turns back and forth, and Pip lists everything he wants to fix this summer.

uncertain.text: The library card may have been in the wallet rather than the tote (low confidence).

2026-07-23.summary: You teach Pip to fix the scooter wheel: bearing cleaned, axle greased, wheel spinning free — and he does the last screw himself while you hold the frame steady.
2026-07-23.one_line: You teach Pip to fix the scooter wheel: bearing cleaned, axle greased, wheel spinning free — and he does the last screw himself while you hold the frame steady.

hl_20260723_1.title: Scooter upside down on the drive
hl_20260723_1.caption: You lay the scooter on its side on a flattened cardboard box and Pip picks the right screwdriver out of the jar by himself.

hl_20260723_2.title: Bearing cleaned, wheel spinning
hl_20260723_2.caption: The bearing was full of grit; after cleaning and a little grease the wheel turns for a long time when Pip spins it.

hl_20260723_3.title: Recording paused while he concentrates
hl_20260723_3.caption: Pip asks you to stop recording while he does the last screw, so you pause and just hold the frame.

hl_20260723_4.title: Checking the chair clamps
hl_20260723_4.caption: Back at the bench the joint has cured square; you check the fit with the multimeter's continuity setting on a hidden screw.

hl_20260723_5.title: Pip rides the fixed scooter
hl_20260723_5.caption: He rides up and down the pavement until the light goes, and Sis pretends not to be impressed but is.

2026-07-24.summary: A storm breaks the heat: you get the last buns before the rain, Dov cooks a huge pot of something, and the four of you play cards at the kitchen table while the windows rattle.
2026-07-24.one_line: A storm breaks the heat: you get the last buns before the rain, Dov cooks a huge pot of something, and the four of you play cards at the kitchen table while the windows rattle.

hl_20260724_1.title: Last buns before the rain
hl_20260724_1.caption: The bakery smells of hot sugar and the cashier says the storm will break the heat by noon, which it does.

hl_20260724_2.title: Dov cooks a very large pot
hl_20260724_2.caption: Dov makes far too much bean stew, and your folded umbrella sits dripping by the back door next to his boots.

hl_20260724_3.title: Storm at the windows
hl_20260724_3.caption: Pip and you shut the upstairs windows just as the rain arrives sideways and the gutters start roaring.

hl_20260724_4.title: Cards at the kitchen table
hl_20260724_4.caption: Four hands of cards, a plate of biscuit crumbs, and the power flickers once and holds.

2026-07-25.summary: Repair cafe with Pip in tow: he learns to hold a screwdriver properly, Tomas gets a radio playing, and you pause recording twice because visitors ask.
2026-07-25.one_line: Repair cafe with Pip in tow: he learns to hold a screwdriver properly, Tomas gets a radio playing, and you pause recording twice because visitors ask.

hl_20260725_1.title: Bench open, toolbox at the end
hl_20260725_1.caption: Fewer fans this week and more small appliances; the mentor sets two visitors up with the screw jar and a cloth.

hl_20260725_2.title: Pip learns the screwdriver
hl_20260725_2.caption: He strips three screws out of a dead kettle and puts them in the jar without being asked twice.

hl_20260725_3.title: Recording paused while someone talks
hl_20260725_3.caption: A visitor wants to explain why the radio matters to her and asks for the glasses to be off; you pause for a while.

hl_20260725_4.title: The radio finally plays
hl_20260725_4.caption: Tomas gets a crackle, then a voice, and Pip claps once, loudly, which makes everyone laugh.

hl_20260725_5.title: Tram home with a tired nephew
hl_20260725_5.caption: Pip falls asleep against the window on line 4 and you carry both bags off at the stop by the bakery.

2026-07-26.summary: Laps at the pool, then the house-sitting handover: bins out, plants watered, keys back on the hook by the door, and your own flat smelling of sawdust when you get home.
2026-07-26.one_line: Laps at the pool, then the house-sitting handover: bins out, plants watered, keys back on the hook by the door, and your own flat smelling of sawdust when you get home.

hl_20260726_1.title: Sunday laps, cooler water
hl_20260726_1.caption: After the storm the water is colder and the coach lets you do a slow, easy set with long rests.

hl_20260726_2.title: Keys back on the hook
hl_20260726_2.caption: Sis comes home to a tidy kitchen; you hang the house keys back on the hook and she hands you a jar of Dov's stew.

hl_20260726_3.title: Bins out, list finished
hl_20260726_3.caption: You cross the last three items off the paper notebook list and Pip adds a drawing of the scooter at the bottom.

hl_20260726_4.title: Home smells of sawdust
hl_20260726_4.caption: Your own flat is hot and smells of sawdust; you open everything, put the lamp on and sit down for a while.

2026-07-27.summary: The oak dresser goes back to Hollis: a final coat of wax, a slow inspection of every drawer, and a handshake at the workshop door in the midday heat.
2026-07-27.one_line: The oak dresser goes back to Hollis: a final coat of wax, a slow inspection of every drawer, and a handshake at the workshop door in the midday heat.

hl_20260727_1.title: Final coat of wax
hl_20260727_1.caption: You wax the runners, check the drawer fronts with the tape measure, and glue one tiny chip back on the corner.

hl_20260727_2.title: Hollis runs a hand along the drawer
hl_20260727_2.caption: Hollis opens and closes every drawer twice, says nothing, then nods and pays the invoice in full.

hl_20260727_3.title: Sandwich and iced coffee
hl_20260727_3.caption: You eat standing at the bakery window and ask the app how many hours the dresser took in total.

hl_20260727_4.title: Tram to the bank and back
hl_20260727_4.caption: A short ride to pay in the cash, wallet in the front pocket, and the tram is packed with people escaping the heat.

hl_20260727_5.title: Ledger lines under the lamp
hl_20260727_5.caption: You write the dresser's hours and payment into the notebook and start a fresh page for August.

2026-07-28.summary: A mending table at the library: you show June how to repair a torn atlas hinge, help two strangers with a broken tote strap, and set a date for the August workshop.
2026-07-28.one_line: A mending table at the library: you show June how to repair a torn atlas hinge, help two strangers with a broken tote strap, and set a date for the August workshop.

hl_20260728_1.title: Mending table by the windows
hl_20260728_1.caption: The holds desk staff push two tables together for you and put out a sign that says bring one broken thing.

hl_20260728_2.title: June's torn atlas endpaper
hl_20260728_2.caption: You show June how to paste a hinge with a thin brush and she does the second one herself, neater than yours.

hl_20260728_3.title: Hinges from the screw jar
hl_20260728_3.caption: Back at the bench you match two old brass hinges out of the jar for Ines's cabinet and set them to soak.

hl_20260728_4.title: Hot tram, windows down
hl_20260728_4.caption: The tram is late and everyone is damp and cheerful; you stand with the tote between your feet and the umbrella hooked on it.

2026-07-29.summary: Cabinet day for Ines: you measure every door, buy hinges at the corner store, and get two squeaking hinges quiet again before the heat makes the workshop unbearable.
2026-07-29.one_line: Cabinet day for Ines: you measure every door, buy hinges at the corner store, and get two squeaking hinges quiet again before the heat makes the workshop unbearable.

hl_20260729_1.title: Measuring every cabinet door
hl_20260729_1.caption: Six doors, three slightly different widths, all written into the notebook with the tape measure snapping shut after each one.

hl_20260729_2.title: Hinges, screws, and a cold drink
hl_20260729_2.caption: You buy four brass hinges and a bag of short screws, pay with the brown wallet, and drink something cold on the walk back.

hl_20260729_3.title: Two hinges quiet again
hl_20260729_3.caption: A drop of glue in the screw holes and a careful tightening takes the squeak out of both; you check nothing binds.

hl_20260729_4.title: Fan, lamp, list
hl_20260729_4.caption: The fan points at the desk, the lamp is on, and you write tomorrow's plan in three short lines.

2026-07-30.summary: Fog on the duck pond in the morning, a slow walk after the bakery, and an evening spent asking the app about repairs from earlier in the year while the town cooled down.
2026-07-30.one_line: Fog on the duck pond in the morning, a slow walk after the bakery, and an evening spent asking the app about repairs from earlier in the year while the town cooled down.

hl_20260730_1.title: Fog sitting on the duck pond
hl_20260730_1.caption: The fog is thick enough that the far bank disappears and the ducks sound closer than they are.

hl_20260730_2.title: Rye and a warm bun
hl_20260730_2.caption: The bakery is the first warm thing of the day and the cashier asks whether the fog will lift before noon.

hl_20260730_3.title: Larsen kids and the ducks
hl_20260730_3.caption: The two kids across the street are feeding the ducks under Mrs. Okafor's supervision until she decides it's too much bread.

hl_20260730_4.title: Asking the app where things went
hl_20260730_4.caption: You ask the app about a missing tape measure and the spare keys, and it finds both: one under the bench, one in the coat pocket.

2026-07-31.summary: Last day of the month: the bakery's final rye, a morning of small jobs at the bench, and an evening with the lamp on, listing August and talking to Sis on the phone.
2026-07-31.one_line: Last day of the month: the bakery's final rye, a morning of small jobs at the bench, and an evening with the lamp on, listing August and talking to Sis on the phone.

hl_20260731_1.title: The month's last rye
hl_20260731_1.caption: The cashier puts the loaf in the bag and says see you Monday, which is a small, good thing.

hl_20260731_2.title: Sweeping out the bench
hl_20260731_2.caption: You sweep the floor, sort the screw jar back into sizes, and put the cafe toolbox by the door for tomorrow.

hl_20260731_3.title: Lamp on, August list
hl_20260731_3.caption: Under the repaired lamp you write a short August list: cabinets, the library workshop, one week off at the end.

hl_20260731_4.title: Call about the next market
hl_20260731_4.caption: Sis calls to plan the next night market and mentions Mrs. Okafor's tomatoes are finally ripening.

2026-08-01.summary: You ride tram line 4 to the repair cafe, fix a desk lamp with the patient mentor, and end the day with a rye loaf from the bakery.
2026-08-01.one_line: You ride tram line 4 to the repair cafe, fix a desk lamp with the patient mentor, and end the day with a rye loaf from the bakery.

hl_20260801_1.title: Tram to the repair cafe
hl_20260801_1.caption: You carry the canvas tote with the multimeter and a lamp base, watching the coast slide past.

hl_20260801_2.title: Lamp wiring with the mentor
hl_20260801_2.caption: The patient volunteer fixer talks you through the loose switch while Tomas tests a radio nearby, and you ask the app to log the repair.

hl_20260801_3.title: Tape measure back on the bench
hl_20260801_3.caption: You find the yellow tape measure under a screw jar and clip it to your apron.

hl_20260801_4.title: Rye loaf for the walk home
hl_20260801_4.caption: The bakery counter slides a warm rye loaf into paper, and you add a cinnamon bun for tomorrow.

hl_20260801_5.title: Tired tram ride home
hl_20260801_5.caption: You balance the tote on your knees, smelling rye bread and feeling the day settle.

uncertain.text: The tape measure may have been left on the cafe bench before you clipped it on (low confidence).
Tomas may have taken the small screwdriver back to his radio table (low confidence).

2026-08-03.summary: Paused: the glasses were away for a hinge repair.

2026-08-04.summary: You spend the day sanding cabinet doors for Ines, make a hardware run for screws, and pause recording during a private client call.
2026-08-04.one_line: You spend the day sanding cabinet doors for Ines, make a hardware run for screws, and pause recording during a private client call.

hl_20260804_1.title: Measuring cabinet doors
hl_20260804_1.caption: You run the yellow tape along each oak door, marking hinge spots with a pencil.

hl_20260804_2.title: Screw jar refill
hl_20260804_2.caption: The corner hardware store sells you a scoop of assorted screws for the cabinet hinges.

hl_20260804_3.title: Ines checks the finish
hl_20260804_3.caption: Ines approves the stain sample and you pause recording while she talks about a family matter.

hl_20260804_4.title: Notes on the tram
hl_20260804_4.caption: You sketch hinge order in the paper notebook and ask the app to remind you about brass screws.

2026-08-05.summary: You return a book to the library, collect a hold, and treat yourself to a bakery cinnamon bun before an afternoon of small repairs at home.
2026-08-05.one_line: You return a book to the library, collect a hold, and treat yourself to a bakery cinnamon bun before an afternoon of small repairs at home.

hl_20260805_1.title: Holds desk pickup
hl_20260805_1.caption: The library holds desk finds your reserved book on wood finishing, and you renew the card for another year.

hl_20260805_2.title: Cinnamon bun break
hl_20260805_2.caption: The bakery counter gives you the last cinnamon bun, still warm in its paper.

2026-09-03.summary: It is the anniversary of your first library card, and the holds desk staff wish you a happy one. You sign up for the accessibility workshop, then find the old card itself in the tote lining at home.

hl_20261026_5.caption: You dry the umbrella, test the multimeter, and leave tomorrow's tote packed.

hl_20261027_1.caption: The holds desk scans your card and hands over a book on simple upholstery.

hl_20261027_2.caption: You read the chalkboard through your glasses and buy a rye roll for lunch.

hl_20261028_2.caption: You set the yellow tape measure against the cabinet door and mark hinge centers.

hl_20261028_6.title: Windy walk from the tram
hl_20261028_6.caption: You lean into the wind with the umbrella closed and the wallet zipped in the tote.

2026-10-29.one_line: A clear, cold walk in the park, a call with your sister about Halloween, and an afternoon of small home repairs with the desk lamp on.

hl_20261029_1.caption: You walk the pond loop with the umbrella as a cane and the glasses on your collar.

hl_20261029_2.title: Bakery rye and buns
hl_20261029_2.caption: The bakery counter bags a rye loaf and two cinnamon buns for the weekend.

hl_20261029_3.caption: You write your sister's trick-or-treat timing in the notebook and agree to mend costumes.

hl_20261029_4.title: Small repairs under the desk lamp
hl_20261029_4.caption: You tighten a drawer pull and read the repair manual under the repaired metal lamp.

hl_20261030_1.caption: Rain hammers the tram roof while the tote holds a cardboard robot arm.

hl_20261030_2.title: Reinforcing a robot costume arm
hl_20261030_2.caption: You add cardboard ribs and glue small screw heads as rivets.

hl_20261030_3.title: Batteries and short screws
hl_20261030_3.caption: You buy batteries for the costume light and a packet of short screws.

hl_20261030_4.title: Private pickup note
hl_20261030_4.caption: Recording pauses while the neighbor explains a family pickup plan; you write only the time.

hl_20261030_5.title: Costume fitting before Halloween
hl_20261030_5.caption: The kids across the street try the robot arm; you glue a loose wrist strap.

hl_20261030_6.title: Candy bowl and dry tote
hl_20261030_6.caption: You set out a bowl of wrapped candy and hang the wet umbrella by the door.

2026-10-31.summary: A short repair cafe morning, then costume repairs for the kids across the street and trick-or-treaters at the door. Recording pauses while children are at the door.

hl_20261031_1.title: Short Halloween cafe bench
hl_20261031_1.caption: You open the red toolbox for a quick morning repair and leave early for costume work.

hl_20261031_2.title: Bakery before costume duty
hl_20261031_2.caption: You buy a rye loaf and a small bag of buns, then tuck the wallet away.

hl_20261031_3.caption: You re-glue wing joints, shorten a strap, and add a soft cloth cuff to the robot arm.

hl_20261031_4.caption: Recording pauses while the neighbor collects the costumes and mentions a private family plan.

hl_20261031_5.title: Trick-or-treaters at the door
hl_20261031_5.caption: You pause recording while children come to the door and hand out wrapped candy from the bowl.

hl_20261031_6.title: Quiet cleanup under the lamp
hl_20261031_6.caption: You sweep glue scraps and switch on the repaired desk lamp after the last knock.

2026-11-01.summary: You swim before the pool fills up, then spend a gray afternoon scrolling back through eleven months of glasses footage, marking the clips worth keeping for a year book.
2026-11-01.one_line: You swim before the pool fills up, then spend a gray afternoon scrolling back through eleven months of glasses footage, marking the clips worth keeping for a year book.

hl_20261101_1.title: Forty lengths before the crowd
hl_20261101_1.caption: Coach counts from the deck and taps the kickboard when you slow down on the last turn.

hl_20261101_2.title: Ducks under a low sky
hl_20261101_2.caption: The pond path is slick with wet leaves and the ducks stay close to the near bank.

hl_20261101_3.title: Eleven months in the timeline
hl_20261101_3.caption: You scrub through January clips and stop on the first repair cafe of the year, cups and screwdrivers everywhere.

hl_20261101_4.title: Keys found under the tote
hl_20261101_4.caption: The app pings the blue tag under a canvas bag by the door, exactly where you left them on Friday.

hl_20261101_5.title: Bench corner tidied
hl_20261101_5.caption: You wipe down the repaired desk lamp and put the paper notebook back where you can find it.

uncertain.text: The locating ping may have come from the spare tag in the toolbox (low confidence).
A February clip may have been skipped while scrolling (low confidence).

2026-11-02.summary: A wet Monday on the tram and at the bench: drawer runners on Hollis's oak dresser, a run to the hardware store for sandpaper, and a quote written up on the sofa.
2026-11-02.one_line: A wet Monday on the tram and at the bench: drawer runners on Hollis's oak dresser, a run to the hardware store for sandpaper, and a quote written up on the sofa.

hl_20261102_1.title: Wet windows on line 4
hl_20261102_1.caption: The tram windows fog at the edges and your umbrella drips into the well by the door.

hl_20261102_2.title: Oak dresser: drawer runners
hl_20261102_2.caption: Two runners are worn hollow, so you plane them flat and test the drawer with the back of your hand.

hl_20261102_3.title: Sandpaper and short screws
hl_20261102_3.caption: You weigh two grades of sandpaper in your hands and add a scoop of short brass screws to the jar.

hl_20261102_4.title: Recording paused for a client's question
hl_20261102_4.caption: Hollis asks about a family piece and you pause the glasses for half an hour, noting it plainly in the timeline.

hl_20261102_5.title: Quote written up on the sofa
hl_20261102_5.caption: You copy measurements from the notebook into a neat estimate and set the reading glasses on the armrest.

2026-11-03.summary: Fog all morning: a rye loaf and cinnamon buns, a holds-desk pickup at the library, and an afternoon of pruning retention settings until only the good clips stay.
2026-11-03.one_line: Fog all morning: a rye loaf and cinnamon buns, a holds-desk pickup at the library, and an afternoon of pruning retention settings until only the good clips stay.

hl_20261103_1.title: Rye loaf and two buns
hl_20261103_1.caption: The counter hands over the warm loaf in a paper bag and warns you the buns are still hot.

hl_20261103_2.title: Holds desk pickup
hl_20261103_2.caption: Two reserved books are waiting and the holds desk scans your card, which still lives in the wallet pocket.

hl_20261103_3.title: Fog on the tram glass
hl_20261103_3.caption: The town slides past in halves, and you get off two stops early just to walk in it.

hl_20261103_4.title: Pruning retention settings
hl_20261103_4.caption: You keep favorites forever and set the rest to thirty days, then hesitate a long while over a folder of workshop clips.

hl_20261103_5.title: Glasses on the shelf
hl_20261103_5.caption: You find the reading glasses on the kitchen shelf, exactly where the app suggested you look.

2026-11-04.summary: Ines brings the reupholstered chairs back for a check, you re-glue a loose frame corner, and a rainy tram ride ends with a call to your sister about Sunday.
2026-11-04.one_line: Ines brings the reupholstered chairs back for a check, you re-glue a loose frame corner, and a rainy tram ride ends with a call to your sister about Sunday.

hl_20261104_1.title: Ines brings the chairs back
hl_20261104_1.caption: She runs a thumb over the new seat edges and asks whether the cabinets could be next.

hl_20261104_2.title: Glue gun on the chair frame
hl_20261104_2.caption: A loose corner gets a careful bead of hot glue and a clamp, and the recording pauses while you hold it steady.

hl_20261104_3.title: Rain drumming on the tram roof
hl_20261104_3.caption: The tram is packed and steamy; you stand with the tote between your feet and watch the harbor go by.

hl_20261104_4.title: Call with Sis about Sunday
hl_20261104_4.caption: She plans a roast and asks whether Pip can bring his broken torch to Saturday's cafe bench.

2026-11-05.summary: Wind all day. You restock the screw jar, take a leaf-blown walk at the park, and lose the yellow tape measure until the app points you back to your own bench.

hl_20261105_1.title: Screw jar refill
hl_20261105_1.caption: You pick through the bins for the sizes you actually use and come out with a heavy paper bag.

hl_20261105_2.title: Scooters on the pond path
hl_20261105_2.caption: Two kids from across the street race past and stop to ask what is in your canvas tote.

hl_20261105_3.title: Tape measure gone missing
hl_20261105_3.caption: You ask the app where the yellow tape was last recorded and it answers: the bench by the window, under a rag.

hl_20261105_4.title: Wind at the windows
hl_20261105_4.caption: The frames rattle and you wedge a folded card into the worst one before making tea.

uncertain.text: Tomas may be the one who borrowed the yellow tape measure last Saturday (low confidence).
One of the two kids on scooters may have been a visitor rather than a neighbour (low confidence).

2026-11-06.one_line: You export a first draft of the year book, scan pages of wiring sketches, and pause recording for twenty minutes at the copy shop when the counter asks you to.

hl_20261106_1.title: Year book draft exported
hl_20261106_1.caption: Eleven months, four hundred clips, and a cover photo of the workshop bench at seven in the morning.

hl_20261106_2.title: Wiring sketches scanned
hl_20261106_2.caption: You photograph page after page of the paper notebook, squinting through the reading glasses at the smudged ones.

hl_20261106_3.title: Tram to the print shop
hl_20261106_3.caption: Recording paused for twenty minutes at the copy shop counter because they asked, and you note it in the timeline.

hl_20261106_4.title: Sorting clips by month
hl_20261106_4.caption: You drag clips into folders and find the whole of March is missing except one wet walk home.

hl_20261106_5.title: Bench tidied before the weekend
hl_20261106_5.caption: Screwdrivers back in the red toolbox, clamps in a row, and the floor swept twice.

2026-11-07.one_line: Saturday at the repair cafe: a stubborn kettle, a lamp socket traced with the January multimeter, and lunch paused at the bakery counter because the cashier asked.

hl_20261107_1.title: Toolbox on the tram
hl_20261107_1.caption: The red toolbox rides on your knees and a stranger asks, kindly, if you are moving house.

hl_20261107_2.title: Setting up the bench
hl_20261107_2.caption: Tomas arranges the radios in a queue by size while you lay out the toolbox and the screw jar.

hl_20261107_3.title: A stubborn kettle
hl_20261107_3.caption: The mentor talks a nervous visitor through a broken switch one small step at a time.

hl_20261107_4.title: Multimeter earns its keep
hl_20261107_4.caption: Your January multimeter traces a dead socket on a table lamp, and you finally feel you got your money's worth.

hl_20261107_5.title: Lunch run, recording paused
hl_20261107_5.caption: You pause at the counter because the cashier asked, and come back with buns and a rye loaf instead of footage.

hl_20261107_6.title: Toolbox packed away
hl_20261107_6.caption: Three fixes out of five, one kettle kept for next week, and the hall swept before four.

uncertain.text: The repaired desk lamp may have been left behind at the bench (low confidence).

2026-11-08.summary: Sunday laps, then a steamy kitchen across town where Dov cooks too much and Pip produces a torch with a dead switch and a plan.

hl_20261108_1.caption: The pool is nearly empty and the coach lets you finish a long set without a word.

hl_20261108_2.title: Dov at the stove
hl_20261108_2.caption: The kitchen windows steam up while he stirs something and insists there is plenty for everyone.

hl_20261108_3.title: Pip's torch
hl_20261108_3.caption: He brings a torch with a dead switch and you promise it a place on Saturday's bench.

hl_20261108_4.title: Recording paused for homework
hl_20261108_4.caption: You pause while Pip reads aloud from a school book, because he asked you not to film him struggling.

hl_20261108_5.title: A year ago today
hl_20261108_5.caption: The timeline offers last November: a foggy tram stop and your first clumsy week of glasses footage.

2026-11-09.summary: A cold start and a long bench day: final wax on the oak dresser, a continuity check on the lamp, and an early night with the timeline left unread.
2026-11-09.one_line: A cold start and a long bench day: final wax on the oak dresser, a continuity check on the lamp, and an early night with the timeline left unread.

hl_20261109_1.title: Cold tram, line 4
hl_20261109_1.caption: Everyone is in winter coats and the tram heater smells faintly of dust.

hl_20261109_2.title: Final wax on the dresser
hl_20261109_2.caption: You work along the grain with the reading glasses pushed up and the radio off.

hl_20261109_3.title: Continuity check on the lamp
hl_20261109_3.caption: The repaired metal desk lamp passes its test again, and you set it aside for the cafe bench.

hl_20261109_4.title: An early night
hl_20261109_4.caption: You leave the day's clips unread and sit with tea and a library book until it gets properly dark.

2026-11-10.summary: The library out of the fog, a chat with June from the January bookbinding class, and an evening searching the app for clips of that first workshop.
2026-11-10.one_line: The library out of the fog, a chat with June from the January bookbinding class, and an evening searching the app for clips of that first workshop.

hl_20261110_1.title: Holds desk returns
hl_20261110_1.caption: You hand back two books and the holds desk stamps the slip without looking up.

hl_20261110_2.title: June from bookbinding
hl_20261110_2.caption: She waves you over to a table of half-finished notebooks and asks if you still keep the paper one.

hl_20261110_3.title: Recording paused for a private story
hl_20261110_3.caption: You pause forty minutes while June talks about something difficult at home, and keep the glasses in your pocket.

hl_20261110_4.title: Searching January clips
hl_20261110_4.caption: You ask the app for January and it hands back a foggy walk and a table of glue brushes.

hl_20261110_5.title: Card back in the wallet
hl_20261110_5.caption: You put the library card where it belongs and the wallet back in the coat pocket.

2026-11-11.summary: Mrs. Okafor brings two split planter boxes to the door and you spend a frosty morning mending them with glue, screws and a fresh bracket, then ride the tram home in the dark.

hl_20261111_1.title: Planters at the front steps
hl_20261111_1.caption: Two boxes have split at the corner and she carries one over herself rather than wait for spring.

hl_20261111_2.title: Screw jar on the bench
hl_20261111_2.caption: You dig out four short screws, run a bead of glue into the split, and clamp it while the kettle boils.

hl_20261111_3.title: Bracket for the planter
hl_20261111_3.caption: You measure twice with the yellow tape, bend a small bracket, and fix it across the weak corner.

hl_20261111_4.title: First frost on the tram roof
hl_20261111_4.caption: The tram windows are clear and cold and the harbour lights come on while you ride home.

2026-11-12.summary: Hollis collects the finished oak dresser, rubbing a hand along the drawer front and asking for a card for a neighbour with a broken chair. The bench feels strangely empty afterwards.
2026-11-12.one_line: Hollis collects the finished oak dresser, rubbing a hand along the drawer front and asking for a card for a neighbour with a broken chair.

hl_20261112_1.title: Dresser ready for pickup
hl_20261112_1.caption: You go over the drawer fronts once more with the glasses on and find nothing left to fix.

hl_20261112_2.title: Hollis collects the dresser
hl_20261112_2.caption: She runs a hand along the drawer front, pays in full, and asks for a card for a neighbour with a broken chair.

hl_20261112_3.title: Ride to the hardware store
hl_20261112_3.caption: You take the tram across town with nothing to carry and enjoy the empty afternoon seats.

hl_20261112_4.title: Hinges and a glue stick
hl_20261112_4.caption: You browse hinges you do not need yet and buy only glue sticks and a box of small screws.

hl_20261112_5.title: An empty bench feeling
hl_20261112_5.caption: With the dresser gone you sit with tea and find the apartment quieter than the workshop.

2026-11-13.summary: A day of second passes: you tighten retention again, print a cover page at the library, and read the year book draft straight through while the export runs overnight.
2026-11-13.one_line: A day of second passes: you tighten retention again, print a cover page at the library, and read the year book draft straight through while the export runs overnight.

hl_20261113_1.title: Retention settings, second pass
hl_20261113_1.caption: You keep repair clips and family clips, delete the rest, and let the export run overnight.

hl_20261113_2.title: Printing the cover page
hl_20261113_2.caption: The holds desk lets you use the printer and the cover photo of the workshop bench comes out slightly too dark.

hl_20261113_3.title: Rye loaf and a bun
hl_20261113_3.caption: You take the loaf for the weekend and eat the bun on the walk to the tram.

hl_20261113_4.title: Notebook pages in the last section
hl_20261113_4.caption: You drop the scanned wiring sketches into the year book's final pages, one drawing per repair.

hl_20261113_5.title: Timeline read-through
hl_20261113_5.caption: You watch a minute of every month in order and find you remember the smells better than the frames.

2026-11-14.summary: The last repair cafe before the winter break: Pip fixes his own torch switch, Tomas clears the radio queue, and the repaired desk lamp finally goes home with a visitor.
2026-11-14.one_line: The last repair cafe before the winter break: Pip fixes his own torch switch, Tomas clears the radio queue, and the repaired desk lamp finally goes home with a visitor.

hl_20261114_1.title: Last cafe before the break
hl_20261114_1.caption: The mentor pins the winter notice to the board while you set out the toolbox for the final Saturday.

hl_20261114_2.title: Pip's torch on the bench
hl_20261114_2.caption: He watches you open the torch with his hands flat on the table and then does the switch himself.

hl_20261114_3.title: Tomas and the radio queue
hl_20261114_3.caption: He gets through three radios and refuses to leave the fourth for the spring.

hl_20261114_4.title: Buns for the volunteers
hl_20261114_4.caption: You pause at the bakery counter because the cashier asked, then carry a bag of buns back to the hall.

hl_20261114_5.title: The lamp goes home at last
hl_20261114_5.caption: A visitor takes the repaired metal desk lamp for a dark hallway and promises to bring the kettle next year.

hl_20261114_6.title: Quick stop for screws
hl_20261114_6.caption: You top up the jar before the shop closes, since the bench will sit quiet until spring.

hl_20261115_1.title: Sun on the pool water
hl_20261115_1.caption: Low sun comes through the high windows and makes bright bands across the lanes.

hl_20261115_2.title: Long loop with Mrs. Okafor
hl_20261115_2.caption: She walks the whole loop beside you with a paper bag of bulbs for the mended planters.

hl_20261115_3.title: Year book export finishes
hl_20261115_3.caption: Eleven minutes of video, forty pages, and a bound copy ordered for the shelf above the bench.

hl_20261115_4.title: Glasses found on the shelf
hl_20261115_4.caption: The app locates the tortoiseshell reading glasses behind the jar of screws, on the shelf above the bench.

hl_20261115_5.title: Last tram of the week
hl_20261115_5.caption: You ride two stops for the air, keys in your pocket, and walk back under a clear cold sky.

uncertain.text: The bound copy may arrive after the winter break (low confidence).

2026-11-17.summary: An errands day: screws and sandpaper, a library hold, an afternoon sanding Ines's cabinet doors, and a long call with Sis after dinner.
2026-11-17.one_line: An errands day: screws and sandpaper, a library hold, an afternoon sanding Ines's cabinet doors, and a long call with Sis after dinner.

hl_20261117_1.title: Packing the tote
hl_20261117_1.caption: You drop the library card and keys into the canvas tote, find the missing tape measure at the bottom, and head out.

hl_20261117_2.title: Screws and 120-grit
hl_20261117_2.caption: A box of 40 mm screws and two sheets of sandpaper; the person at the counter asks what you're building and you say, a dresser.

hl_20261117_3.title: Holds desk pickup
hl_20261117_3.caption: The holds desk hands over a joinery manual, and you ask the app what that book on shellac finishes was called back in March.

hl_20261117_4.title: Radio cord and Ines's chair seats
hl_20261117_4.caption: You test the power cord of a radio Tomas might want for Saturday, then start sanding the cabinet doors Ines left last week.

hl_20261117_5.title: A bent planter bracket
hl_20261117_5.caption: Mrs. Okafor waves you over about a bent bracket on her planter; you pause recording while she shows you photos on her phone.

hl_20261117_6.title: Call with Sis about Sunday
hl_20261117_6.caption: Sis asks if you'll come for lunch Sunday and whether Pip can visit the workshop; you say yes to lunch, maybe to the workshop.

2026-11-18.summary: You spend the foggy Wednesday inside your own archive: scrolling a year of clips, printing a year book at the library, and cutting retention settings down to what you actually want to keep.
2026-11-18.one_line: You spend the foggy Wednesday inside your own archive: scrolling a year of clips, printing a year book at the library, and cutting retention settings down to what you actually want to keep.

hl_20261118_1.title: A year of tram rides, one thumb
hl_20261118_1.caption: Fog on the windows; you scrub the timeline back to January and see a year of line 4 mornings stacked in rows.

hl_20261118_2.title: Marking the keepers
hl_20261118_2.caption: You star the clips worth keeping: the desk lamp coming back to life, Pip's first repair, Hollis's dresser sliding shut.

hl_20261118_3.title: The year book, printed and bound
hl_20261118_3.caption: At the library print corner you run off ninety pages and spiral-bind them; the holds desk staff admires the cover page.

hl_20261118_4.title: Trimming retention settings
hl_20261118_4.caption: You ask the app how many Saturdays you spent at the repair cafe, then set shop clips to delete after ninety days and starred ones to stay.

hl_20261118_5.title: Finding the notebook
hl_20261118_5.caption: You ask where the paper notebook was last seen; the app points to the desk, and it's under the lamp, just off the edge.

hl_20261118_6.title: Showing Pip the year book
hl_20261118_6.caption: On a video call Pip asks for the page with the duck pond and the page with the glue gun, and Sis says she wants a copy.
